reply_text:
㊥ (do the keywords detect anything?) Yes, and on the held-out turns they agree with an independent judge better than chance. This is the first time any route this week has. Of the 150 turns no elaborating agent saw, 96 trigger at least one R-node. On the 61 of those that also have a turn bid from the R-node agents, a detected node is among the bid nodes 39% of the time, against 22% by chance. That's with a plain word matcher: no model, just the 440 cues from the tree and the three elaborations.

㊢ (on all your recent turns) Across all 1,226 operator turns in the live annotation store, 63% trigger at least one node:

| Nodes per turn | Share of turns |
|---|---:|
| 0 | 37% |
| 1 | 26% |
| 2 | 17% |
| 3 or more | 20% |

The counts do look odd, as you anticipated:
- **R4 (forward model):** 32% of turns, and "would" alone fires on 22%.
- **R16 (enactment):** 26%, mostly "work".
- **R1 (belief):** 16%, mostly "I think".
- **R6 (options):** 17%, mostly "we could".
- **Assurance nodes:** almost invisible. R9 is on 7 turns, R12 on 3, R10 on 3, R3a on 1.

So a handful of everyday words carry most of the volume. The assurance side either has the wrong cues or rarely shows up in your wording.

㊬ (with the everyday words removed) I reran without 12 of them: "would", "work", "will", "I think", "we could", "build", "design", "until", "if we", "rather … than", "level", "enough". Detection drops to 55 of 150 held-out turns. Agreement with the turn bids holds at 33%, against 15% by chance. Removing those words gives up coverage, but what remains is more specific.

㊭ (what I'd look at next) Two things the counts suggest, before touching the tree:
1. **Everyday words:** make them count only when they occur with something more specific. For example, "would" counts towards R4 only alongside "if" or a named consequence.
2. **Assurance nodes:** look at turns where you are clearly checking or auditing, and see what words you actually use there. The agents' cues for R9 and R12 ("independent", "calibrated") seem to be words you rarely write.

Everything is in futon0 `de2866c`, `rnode-tree/DETECT-2026-10-02.md`, including the 40 cues that fire most often.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(how much they agree) The script keeps 208 cues. It dropped 2 from Codex and 3 from zai-4 because the quote wasn't in the cited turn. Exact-wording overlap is tiny: only 2 cues are proposed in the same words for the same node. Comparing by turn is fairer. 35 development turns are cited by both agents. On 16 of them they name a shared node, and on 19 they name only different nodes. The disagreements cluster in three places:
- **R13 vs CTAU-CLASS:** T004 and T026, "work in the dependency order". Is ordering the work planning depth, or a preference schedule?
- **R2 vs R10 and R8:** T095 and T221, "now I see … it only executes the sleep command". Is that an observation, a liveness check, or a mismatch?
- **R14 vs R15, R16 and R6:** T238 and T247, "Let's go with the exporter".

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(other flags) Each of these was raised by one agent only:
- **R7 to Understanding·Having** (Codex): source reliability is held information, not a disposition to participate. I think this is right.
- **R12 to Understanding·Doing** (Codex): calibration is an activity.
- **R9 to Protection·Doing** (Codex).
- **R17 toward System 5** (zai-4): restructuring the framework's own categories is identity work.
- **R19** (Codex): notes that the catalogue's PERCEIVE stage label doesn't match its System 5 placement.
